Yes, in Next.js App Router, the 'use client' directive must be a literal first statement in the module to mark a Client Component. It must appear at the very beginning of the file, as a string literal ('use client' or "use client", not backticks), before any imports or other code (comments are allowed before it). Official Next.js documentation consistently shows it as the first line in examples, e.g.: 'use client' import { useState } from 'react' ... The React documentation explicitly states: "'use client' must be at the very beginning of a file, above any imports or other code (comments are OK). They must be written with single or double quotes, but not backticks." Issues arise if not placed correctly, such as Next.js not recognizing it or syntax errors, confirming the strict positioning.

Citations:

- 1: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-client
- 2: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

<details>
<summary>🧩 Analysis chain</summary>

🌐 Web query:

`In Worktrunk hook documentation, what arguments/environment variables are provided to the `pre-remove` hook, and how should a hook determine the exact branch/worktree being removed?`

💡 Result:

In Worktrunk hook documentation, the pre-remove hook is provided with template variables (not traditional environment variables) that can be interpolated into hook commands defined in TOML config files (.config/wt.toml or ~/.config/worktrunk/config.toml). These variables are also passed as JSON on stdin to hook scripts for programmatic access. Key template variables available to pre-remove hooks, which reference the worktree being removed: - {{ branch }}: Active branch name (the branch being removed) - {{ worktree_path }}: Active worktree path (path of the worktree being removed) - {{ worktree_name }}: Active worktree directory name - {{ commit }}: Active branch HEAD SHA - {{ short_commit }}: Active branch HEAD SHA (7 chars) - Plus others like {{ repo_path }}, {{ repo }}, {{ default_branch }}, etc. To determine the exact branch/worktree being removed, use {{ branch }} for the branch name and {{ worktree_path }} for the full path. The hook runs in the worktree being removed (cwd is the worktree root), providing direct file access before deletion. Example config: [pre-remove] archive = "tar -czf ~/.wt-logs/{{ branch }}.tar.gz test-results/ logs/ 2>/dev/null || true" Here, {{ branch }} expands to the branch name (e.g., "feature-auth"), identifying the worktree. pre-remove is blocking: failure aborts removal. It runs before worktree deletion during wt remove or wt merge --remove.

Citations:

- 1: https://worktrunk.dev/hook/
- 2: https://worktrunk.dev/worktrunk/

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

<details>
<summary>🧩 Analysis chain</summary>

🌐 Web query:

`What are the current platform compatibility requirements for `@electric-sql/pglite`, specifically Electron version requirements for SharedArrayBuffer and support status for Tauri, browser extensions (MV3), React Native/Expo, Node.js, Bun, and Deno?`

💡 Result:

Current platform compatibility for `@electric-sql/pglite` (as of 2026-03-28): - Electron: Works via Node.js filesystem APIs (file:// or unprefixed dataDir). SharedArrayBuffer requires Electron v11.0+ with appropriate flags (e.g., --enable-features=SharedArrayBuffer), but not explicitly required by PGlite; uses standard Node FS. Multi-tab worker support in progress (open issue `#398`). - Tauri: No explicit mention; likely works as it supports Node-like FS and WASM, but unconfirmed. - Browser extensions (MV3): No explicit support mentioned; browser-compatible but MV3 service worker restrictions may limit persistence (IndexedDB ok, OPFS limited). - React Native/Expo: Not supported. Open issue `#87` tracks progress; depends on libpglite native build. Experimental user attempts exist but buggy/not production-ready. Electric docs confirm PGlite doesn't work in RN yet. - Node.js: Fully supported (file system persistence). - Bun: Fully supported (file system persistence). - Deno: Fully supported (file system persistence). Official docs emphasize browser (IndexedDB), Node/Bun/Deno. Requires Node v20+ for building.

Citations:

- 1: https://github.com/electric-sql/pglite
- 2: https://electric-sql.com/primitives/pglite
- 3: https://electric-sql.com/product/pglite
